records.rationale: Complete five-path/76-addition original patch read and all seven hook families traced to final sites/declarations/exports. Keep RT placement, fallback, ordinary renamed final tick, pre-class flagged enqueue/dequeue, migration veto and evolved proxy-aware lowest-rq callbacks. Old disabled stubs/CREATE_TRACE_POINTS placement are superseded by final common plumbing. CPU fallback and common class selector guarded in e496198e4e74. RT lowest-rq override now guarded in f579492cb154 for range, active CPU, and nullable execution-context cpus_mask, preserving native cpupri filtering rather than allowing callback to undo it. Keep valid alternative CPU preference, including when native priority search returned no result; caller priority checks and retry remain. Event-order/default-body details are in cross-linked completed reviews. No historical binary KMI, removed restricted tick name, platform-specific vendor scheduler or runtime performance claim is introduced.

updated_prior_decision.rationale: Both original signature/call paths read in rt-dl-chain-review. Retain donor scheduling context and nullable execution context in restricted find_lowest_rq event, with initialized -1 output. Later adaptation f579492cb154 validates nonnegative callback output for range, active CPU, and execution-context cpus_mask before returning it. NULL execution context does not impose donor affinity, matching cpupri semantics. Callback still controls candidate preference and must respect borrowed mask/lifetime and caller locking; no arbitrary callback safety or exact SDK consumer is established.

caller_analysis.select_task_rq_rt: Uses target in fitness and cpu_rq(target) before common select_task_rq final guard, requiring range enforcement inside find_lowest_rq. Rechecks lower destination priority; common selector later enforces final task constraints.
caller_analysis.find_lock_lowest_rq: After -1/current rejection obtains cpu_rq(cpu), checks destination priority, locks rq pair, revalidates task/chain after lock drop and retries. Output must already be in range and meet active/execution-affinity requirement. Existing optimistic priority races remain handled by native/port retries.
caller_analysis.push_rt_task: Migration-disabled path asks whether rq donor/current has another suitable CPU, then obtains push task and schedules stopper. Does not grant callback ownership of rq/task references.
caller_analysis.cpupri: __cpupri_find masks candidates with execution context cpus_mask if non-NULL, then cpu_active_mask (earlier adaptation preserves this native active filter). NULL means no execution affinity restriction, not donor affinity; new guard matches that distinction.

compatibility: Valid vendor alternative CPU preferences remain, including an override after ret=0, because priority/fitness customization is intentional. Active/range/execution-affinity violations now fall back to native selector. Lowest-mask pointer stays mutable/trusted and there is no blanket validation of a callback corrupting it.
security: Before this guard a nonnegative hook result could reach cpu_rq/per-CPU softirq helpers out of bounds and bypass an LTS-preserved active/affinity filter. Restore those constraints before consumption without replacing the proxy-aware implementation with old ACK code. No actual kernel crash, hotplug race, priority inversion bound or malicious-module protection is claimed.
validation: 57600 extracted-function host cases pass. Previous control returns ineligible CPU in 7744; selector itself does not dereference those results, but callers do. CPUpri eligibility, topology distribution, RCU and locking are modeled; no runtime verification. Build 139 pending after build 138 completes.
